answer: In an agent market selling canyon maps, zephyr forecasts, and shale assays, access to paid jobs is proportional to collateral locked for 30 days, not the number of accounts. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities therefore earns no extra allocation. To capture more jobs, an attacker must lock proportionally more capital, forgoing its use elsewhere; collateral is slashed if an agent fails a contract’s verifiable delivery test.
